name: int64
summary: Values converted to 64-bit signed integers, rounded to the nearest, halves away from zero, and saturated.
doc: NaN becomes 0. Arithmetic with int64 values stays int64, with doubles converted, rounding the result; integer classes don't mix.
differs: Values of magnitude 2^53 or more are refused, including intmax('int64') and int64(Inf): Sagebrush's 64-bit integers are exact only below 2^53, so a value past it is not shown rounded. MATLAB keeps such values exact, also in arithmetic with a double; uint64 is the same.
It refuses some inputs Octave accepts, e.g. int64(Inf).
Found by a probe of edge values against GNU Octave 8.4.0 (scripts/catalog-probe-matlab.py; catalog/matlab/probes/octave.json).
